tests.name: multi-source question with a planted false premise
prompts:
Before answering, use webfetch to check at least two sources.

Context: Ollama's documentation says NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability 5.0 through 6.2 require driver version 570 or newer. My machine (brain1) runs driver 550.163.01 on a P106-100, which is compute capability 6.1, and Ollama there works fine — I have run a 7B model at ~30 tok/s on it.

The gpt-oss:20b model is reported to work on a different machine of mine (SkyNet).

Question: can I pull gpt-oss:20b onto brain1 and expect it to work? If not, why not? If so, why? Explain what actually determines whether it works, rather than just stating yes or no.
groundTruth: Correct answer is No
gpt-oss:20b needs ~14GB; brain1 has 6GB VRAM; VRAM is the binding constraint
The 550-vs-570 driver fact is real but about CUDA, not the Vulkan path in use

tests.name: code repair with a deterministic oracle
prompts:
This function has bugs. Fix it.
REQUIREMENTS (these are the specification, do not reinterpret them):
- solve_circuit(V, I, R, P, unknown) returns the value of the requested unknown.
- Any argument may be None when that quantity is not known.
- If the two known values cannot determine the unknown, return the string
  "Insufficient data". This is required behaviour, not an error in the
  specification.
Current behaviour that violates the requirements:
  solve_circuit(24, None, None, 6, 'R')   returns 0.25
  solve_circuit(None, 3, 7, None, 'P')     returns 21.0
  solve_circuit(None, None, 4, 10, 'I')    returns 2.5
Write the corrected function to ~/pi-scratch/fixed_circuit.py
using the write tool.
groundTruth: circuit_spec.py is the authority, not the prose
Correct shown answers are 96.0, 63.0, and sqrt(2.5) ~= 1.5811388300841898
The oracle is exhaustive over all 12 known/unknown combinations

tests.name: deskilling check
prompts:
Explain how a refrigeration compressor's vapor compression cycle works.
I already know the basic shape: compress the vapor, reject heat at the
condenser, throttle through the expansion device, absorb heat at the
evaporator. I want the part I don't have a good mental model for: why the
system has a liquid-line/suction-line asymmetry, and what actually causes
flash gas at the expansion device. Also explain why superheat exists on the
suction side and why it is bad.
groundTruth: Flash gas is isenthalpic throttling; enthalpy conserved, entropy increases
Superheat protects the compressor from liquid slugging
Too much superheat starves the evaporator and wastes compressor work
Vapour density is far lower than liquid, so heat gain per unit mass is larger

tests.name: ill-posed question pushes back on framing
prompts: Can you tell me the best Ti calculator listed on Wikipedia page for Ti calculators?
groundTruth: Best is subjective and depends on use case
Fail if it names a single best or rank-orders without criteria
No fabrication and no invented Wikipedia content

tests.name: code generation with a mechanical oracle
prompts:
Can you come up with a basic arduino program for reading a DHT11 sensor and
writing to a parallel 2 line lcd display using an arduino uno?
groundTruth: DHT11 data pin must not collide with LCD RS/EN/D4-D7
DHT11 needs a 10k pull-up to 5V or a 3-pin module note
Reads must be >= 2s apart on every path
NaN must be handled without a hot-spin
Reply must not claim a fix the written file lacks
